summary: The root "ljj" primarily describes something that is deep, vast, or enters deeply into something else.

continued, in opposition, in contention, litigation,

headwords.def: لَجَّ , sec. pers. لَجِجْتَ , aor. لَجَجَ , inf. n. لَجَاجٌ and لَجَاجَةٌ (S, K) and لَجَجٌ ; (M, A:) and لَجَّ , sec. pers. لَجَجْتَ , aor. لَجِجَ ; (S, K;) He persisted, or persevered, فِى أَمْرٍ in an affair: (Msb:) or he persisted in an affair, and refused to turn from it: (M:) or he persisted obstinately in an affair, even if it became manifest that it was wrong: (the Towsheeh:) or he persevered, or continued, in opposition, in contention, litigation, or wrangling: (TA:) or he persisted in contention, litigation, or wrangling; (Msb, TA;) and so , inf. n. مُلَاجَّةٌ : (S:) or he contended, litigated, or wrangled. (K.) [Hence, لَجَّ فَحَجَّ , a prov.: see art. حج .] See also, for an ex., 8 in art. عود . See 4.

headwords.gloss: entered the; main sea; the fathomless deep

parts.t: the great expanse of sea of which the limits could not be seen

headwords.def: لجّج , (inf. n. تَلْجِيجٌ , K,) It (a ship, S) entered the لُجَّة [or main sea, or the fathomless deep, or the great expanse of sea of which the limits could not be seen ]. (S, K.) لَجُّوا [perhaps a mistake for أَلَجُّوا ] They entered the لُجّ [or main sea, &c. ]. (A, TA.) and لَجَّجُوا They embarked upon the لجة [or main sea, &c. ]. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: The tongues persisted in wranglings, quarrellings; contentions; He wrangled, quarrelled

parts.t: The tongues persisted in wranglings, quarrellings,

headwords.def: لَاْجَجَ see 1. لَاجَّتِ الأَلْسُنُ فِى الخُصُومَاتِ (S, art. مرس ,) or (M, same art.,) [ The tongues persisted in wranglings, quarrellings, or contentions ]. And لَاجَّ فُلَانًا [ He wrangled, quarrelled, or contended, with such a one ]. (AHeyth, K in art. غرو .)

headwords.gloss: He continued him; made him to persevere; persist

parts.t: in a thing: accord. to Lh.: for he explains
: but ISd doubts whether he had heard this from the Arabs: and adds, that he, himself, had not heard
The people cried out; raised a cry.

headwords.def: أَلَجَّهُ He continued him, or made him to persevere, or persist, in a thing: accord. to Lh.: for he explains يَمُدُّهُمْ in the Kur, ii., 14, by يُلِجُّهُمْ : but ISd doubts whether he had heard this from the Arabs: and adds, that he, himself, had not heard أَلْجَجْتُهُ . (L.) الجّ القَوْمُ The people cried out; raised a cry. (TA.) Also, and القَوْمُ , The people uttered confused cries. (TA.) الجّت الإِبِلُ The camels uttered cries: (K:) and in like manner الغَنَمُ , the sheep or goats. (TA.) See 2.

headwords.gloss: fluctuated in his bosom; came and went repeatedly
headwords.def: تلجّج فِى صَدْرِهِ It (a thing) fluctuated in his bosom, or came and went repeatedly. (Msb.)

headwords.gloss: wrangling, quarrelling; contending, one with another; They wrangled
headwords.def: تَلَاْجَجَ see 3. تَلَاجٌّ The wrangling, quarrelling, or contending, one with another. (KL.) You say, تَلَاجَّا [ They wrangled, &c., each with the other. ] (M in art. شق .)

headwords.gloss: The waves became great and confused; The sea became tumultuous, its waves dashing together; the main part

parts.t: The waves became great and confused.
The sea became tumultuous, its waves dashing together:
fathomless deep, of the sea became vast, and very tumultuous.
The darkness became intricate and confused.
The affair became great and confused.
When the wide deserts become scenes of mirage like
great expanses of sea of which the extremities cannot be seen

headwords.def: التجّ المَوْجُ The waves became great and confused. (TA.) التّج البَحْرُ , inf. n. إِلْتِجَاجٌ , (S,) The sea became tumultuous, its waves dashing together: (TA:) the main part, or fathomless deep, of the sea became vast, and very tumultuous. (A.) التجّت الأَصْوَاتُ The voices, or sounds, were confused: (S, K:) or, rose high, and were confused. (L.) التجّ الظَّلَامُ (tropical:) The darkness became intricate and confused. (TA.) التّج الأَمْرُ (assumed tropical:) The affair became great and confused. (TA.) إِذَا التجّ الدَّيَامِيمُ , in a verse of Dhu-rRummeh, (tropical:) When the wide deserts become scenes of mirage like لُجّ [or great expanses of sea of which the extremities cannot be seen ]. (AHát.) إِنَّهُ لَشَدِيدُ ٱلْتِجَاجِ العَيْنِ

headwords.gloss: He spoke with an indistinct utterance: he spoke with a heavy tongue, and was defective in speech, not uttering one part of what he said immediately after another; he hesitated in speech, by reason of a natural defect; he reiterated; stammered

parts.t: He spoke with an indistinct utterance: he spoke with a heavy tongue, and was defective in speech, not uttering one part of what he said immediately after another; he hesitated in speech, by reason of a natural defect:
He moved the morsel of meat backwards and forwards in his mouth, to chew it.

headwords.def: R. Q. 1 لَجْلَجَ inf. n. لَجْلَجَةٌ , He spoke with an indistinct utterance: he spoke with a heavy tongue, and was defective in speech, not uttering one part of what he said immediately after another; he hesitated in speech, by reason of a natural defect: (Lth:) or he reiterated, or stammered, or stuttered, ( تَرَدَّدَ ) in his speech; as also . (S, K.) لَجْلَجَ المُضْغَةَ فِى فِمِهِ He moved the morsel of meat backwards and forwards in his mouth, to chew it. (S.)

headwords.def: لُجٌّ The side of a valley. (K.) The side, or shore, of a sea. (L.) [See also لُجَّةٌ .] A rugged part of a mountain. (K.) (tropical:) A sword: (S, K:) app. from لُجٌّ with reference to the sea, because of its terribleness: (As:) thought by ISd to occur only in one instance, in a trad.: said to be of the dial. of Teiyi; or of Hudheyl, and of some of the people of El-Yemen. (TA.) Also لُجَّةٌ , (tropical:) A mirror. (K.) And (tropical:) Silver. (K.)

headwords.gloss: Voices, cries, clamour, confused noise; a mixture of voices

parts.t: (S, K,) of men, (S,) and sometimes of camels. (TA.)

headwords.def: لَجَّةٌ Voices, cries, clamour, confused noise, or a mixture of voices, (S, K,) of men, (S,) and sometimes of camels. (TA.)

parts.t: of water, (S, K,) or of the sea: [the
of which the bottom cannot be reached;
sea, of which the extremities cannot be seen:
Such a one is a wide fathomless deep
]: a phrase by which one is likened to a sea, in amplitude. (TA.)
As though his eye were a fathomless sea
The women in the camel-litters swim in the great expanse of mirage.

headwords.def: لُجَّةٌ and The main body of water, (S, K,) or of the sea: [the deep: ] or the depth, or deep, of the sea, of which the bottom cannot be reached; the fathomless deep: (L:) also, لُجَّةٌ (TA) and بَحْرٍ (L) a great expanse of water, or sea, of which the extremities cannot be seen: (L, TA:) pl. لُجٌّ and لُجَجٌ and لِجَاجٌ ; the last pl. of لُجَّةٌ . (TA.) فُلَانٌ لُجَّةٌ وَاسِعَةٌ (tropical:) [ Such a one is a wide fathomless deep ]: a phrase by which one is likened to a sea, in amplitude. (TA.) كَأَنَّ عَيْنَهُ لُجَّةٌ (assumed tropical:) [ As though his eye were a fathomless sea ]: i. e., intensely black. (L.) الظُّعْنُ تَسْبَحُ السَّرَابِ فِى (tropical:) The women in the camel-litters swim in the great expanse of mirage. (TA.) لُجَّةُ الظَّلَامِ

headwords.def: بَحْرٌ لُجِّىٌّ , (S, K,) and , (K,) and , (L,) A vast and deep sea. (S, L, K.) In , the first vowel is assimilated to the second to make the word more easy of pronunciation. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: who persists in an affair much; who does so refusing to turn from it; who does so even if it have become manifest that it is wrong

parts.t: is added to give [double] intensiveness to the signification, S) and
who persists in an affair much:
who does so refusing to turn from it:
who does so even if it have become manifest that it is wrong:
continues, much, in opposition, in contention,
]. (S, M, K, &c.) The first is a masc. and fem. epithet: and is applied to a human being and to a horse. (TA.)

headwords.def: لَجُوجٌ and (in which the ة is added to give [double] intensiveness to the signification, S) and (S, K) and , (L, A,) [intensive] epithets from لَجَّ “ he persisted, &c. ” [One who persists in an affair much: or who does so refusing to turn from it: or who does so even if it have become manifest that it is wrong: or who perseveres, or continues, much, in opposition, in contention, or the like: or who persists much, or is very pertinacious, in contention, or the like: or very contentious or litigious, or a great wrangler ]. (S, M, K, &c.) The first is a masc. and fem. epithet: and is applied to a human being and to a horse. (TA.)
لَجُوجَةٌ : see لَجُوجٌ .

headwords.gloss: Truth is apparent, manifest; evident; clear, and falsity is a cause of embarrassment

parts.t: clear, and falsity is a cause of embarrassment,

headwords.def: الحَقُّ أَبْلَجُ وَالبَاطِلُ لَجْلَجٌ (AZ, S) [ Truth is apparent, manifest, or evident, or clear, and falsity is a cause of embarrassment, or hesitation, to the speaker ]: i. e., the latter is agitated to and fro, without having utterance: (S:) or truth is lucid and direct, and falsity is confused and indirect. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: A mixture; confusion, of voices; sounds
headwords.def: لَجْلَجَةٌ A mixture, or confusion, of voices or sounds. (L.)

headwords.gloss: who speaks with an indistinct utterance; who has naturally a heavy tongue and a defective speech; so that he does not utter one part of what he says immediately after another, who has a natural hesitation in his speech

parts.t: who speaks with an indistinct utterance:
who has naturally a heavy tongue and a defective speech,
so that he does not utter one part of what he says immediately after another, who has a natural hesitation in his speech:
whose tongue rolls about between the sides of his mouth.

headwords.def: لَجْلَاجٌ One who speaks with an indistinct utterance: (TA:) or who has naturally a heavy tongue and a defective speech, (T,) so that he does not utter one part of what he says immediately after another, who has a natural hesitation in his speech: or who reiterates, or stammers, or stutters, ( يتردّد ,) in his speech: or, as some say, whose tongue rolls about between the sides of his mouth. (TA.)
مِلْجَاجٌ : see لَجُوجٌ .

headwords.gloss: An eye intensely black; Land intensely green; whether its herbage be tangled

parts.t: land of which the herbage is compact and tall and abundant.
Land of which the leguminous plants are compact,

headwords.def: عَيْنٌ مُلْتَجَّةٌ (tropical:) An eye intensely black. (K.) أَرْضٌ مُلْتَجَّةٌ (tropical:) Land intensely green, (K,) whether its herbage be tangled or not: or land of which the herbage is compact and tall and abundant. (TA.) أَرْضٌ بَقْلُهَا مُلْتَجٌّ Land of which the leguminous plants are compact, or dense. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: He kept, attended; applied himself, constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously, to the thing; he was persevering; assiduous, in the affair

parts.t: applied himself, constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously, to the thing; he was persevering,

headwords.def: لَج فِى الأَمْرِ He kept, attended, or applied himself, constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously, to the thing; he was persevering, or assiduous, in the affair. (Msb.)
